electrical_order.encoder: Protocol index 0 broadcasts both; logical indices 1/2 address separate lamps. Current QEMU led-rgb[0]/[1] correspond to those logical selections. Diagram is PA0 -> LED1 -> LED2, but no inspected PCB/placement source ties these to model left/right. Public firmware C source is unavailable in inspected tree.
electrical_order.8encoder: Pinned main.c register 0x70+3*i feeds neopixel_set_color(i); ws2812_show serializes ascending i. Schematic chain input is U1, then U2...U9. Circuit-symbol positions (drawn right to left on the schematic) are not PCB physical placement. No U1-U9 -> CH1-CH8/switch table was found.

ready_subset.scope: uniform/all-off LED readback only; no logical-index to physical-target permutation is claimed

readback came from real guest controller output; do not synthesize source-side answers
ready_subset.condition: len(colors)==2 and all(type(x) is int and 0<=x<=0xFFFFFF for x in colors) and len(set(colors))==1
ready_subset.nonuniform_policy: Do not set an identity ledTargets binding or select the first color. Mark the visual mapping unavailable. A stale previous uniform glow must not be presented as current output; neutralize/hide it with explicit unavailable semantics, not a claim that electrical LEDs are off.
ready_subset.validation_required: Visible Device Service session + original driver + real mounted Led material and Encoder shell-diffusion uniforms. Red/green/blue/all-off transitions and uniform -> asymmetric -> uniform; 3D or material assertions required. This research has not run that validation.

encoder.official_example: bundled UIFlow angle=(get_rotary_value()/58)*360; visual screen circle example, not a physical calibration record
encoder.source_interface: runtime profile injects counter directly; tracked C patch sets s->counter[0] within signed16 range. No independent shaft/source field or phase pins.
encoder.software_offsets: UIFlow set_rotary_value/reset_rotary_value only change Python instance offsets. Current C accepts mode/RGB writes, not counter writes/reset. Do not attribute 8Encoder guest-reset behavior to Encoder.
encoder.unresolved: actual physical PPR vs decoder multiplier, mode behavior, installed CW sign, rollover semantics and neutral reference

electrical_phase_semantics.precondition: AB mode g_mode_sel=0; clean accepted single-bit edges passing firmware debounce; phases expressed as (A,B)
electrical_phase_semantics.evidence: A-branch uses prior g_phase_a_last_encoder_status at lines 730..753, toggled after switch at 942. B-branch uses prior B state at 986..1009, toggled at 1198. Both phases configured rising/falling at 1468..1473.
electrical_phase_semantics.limit: This is electrical phase-sequence sign in pinned source only. No installed-part PPR, physical front-view CW/CCW sign or physical timing follows.

8encoder.part_identity: schematic labels only EC11A; exact manufacturer/variant, PPR/detents/phase relation to front-view CW remain unavailable
8encoder.source_interface: runtime injects counters array directly. C uses same counter array for guest writable 0x00..0x1F and reset 0x40..0x47, so guest reset changes the value frontend would currently use as angle. No independent immutable physical source.
8encoder.required_behavior: A guest set/reset must not rotate the visual shaft. Source movement must update electrical/controller count through a separately defined source contract. A scale/offset from mutable counters alone is insufficient.

smallest_missing_official_sources.minimal: One annotated assembly/placement view or pick-and-place CSV per product revision containing LED1/LED2 or U1..U9 XY/side, Grove orientation and optical aperture/channel correspondence. A complete PCB/Gerber project is unnecessary if that small table is authoritative.
smallest_missing_official_sources.alternative: Reproducible original-driver physical one-hot LED capture with fixed firmware hash and front/Grove orientation: Encoder two single-lamp selections; 8Encoder nine single-index selections. No such physical test performed here.

smallest_missing_official_sources.minimal: Exact installed encoder manufacturer and full part suffix/datasheet PPR, decoder mode/multiplication, and mounted A/B-to-front-CW direction.
